title: Trip-confidence windows, probe rejoin policy, and safe fallback plumbing
creator: Priya Desai
description: Propose and implement a conservative, measurable circuit tripping and rejoin strategy that is safe for multi-tenant, multi-model, and multi-region inference paths. Goals: (1) avoid noisy/over-aggressive trips when sample sizes are small, (2) ensure trips align with SLO burn-rate and business impact, (3) provide deterministic staged reintroduction of routes with low risk of cascading outages, and (4) wire fallback plumbing so callers get transparent, bounded behavior (compatible model variant, cached prefix response, or explicit 429/503 with guidance).
acceptance_criteria: 1) New breaker config supports trip-confidence window and min-samples; 2) Trip reasons recorded with confidence score and sample counts; 3) Rejoin policy implements staged probes (0.1% -> 1% -> 10% -> full) with backoff on failures; 4) Fallback mappings exist for model->compatible-variant and for tenant->graceful-degrade pages; 5) End-to-end e2e test and chaos simulation validating no more than 3x SLO burn during recovery for impacted tenants; 6) Dashboard and alerting templates added to Console release runtime-1.24.
design_decisions: - Use a hybrid metric for trips: weighted error rate + tail-latency signal (p95+p99) combined into a single "incident_score" normalized to SLO targets. - Apply Bayesian smoothing (Jeffreys prior) with configurable min_samples to prevent short-lived spikes from tripping. - Trip when incident_score exceeds configured threshold for an observation window AND burn-rate estimate > 1.5x target. - Differentiate scopes: per-dependency (service), per-model, per-tenant; each scope has independent counters and hierarchical override rules. - Rejoin uses staged probe percentages with exponential backoff and minimum probe-success ratio to progress. - Fallbacks chosen from prioritized list: cached-prefix-response -> always-available-compatible-quantized-variant -> regional-fallback-model -> fail-open with graceful 429 + guidance. - Expose observability: reason, sample_count, success_rate, p99, incident_score, confidence_interval in traces and metrics.
implementation_notes: - Data plane: extend per-request context to emit lightweight trip telemetry and scope tags (region, tenant_id, model_variant). - Sliding window aggregator runs in runtime sidecar; uses reservoir sampling for long tails and retains per-scope histograms for latency quantiles. - Storage: use high-cardinality metrics in TSDB (prometheus-remote) with rollups; also emit OTel logs for detailed incident traces. - Config API: support rule objects with fields: scope, min_samples, window_sec, incident_threshold, burn_rate_multiplier, probe_schedule (list of percentages and min_successes). Example rule snippet included below. - Backstop: global guardian that can open a universal safety gate under platform-wide overload detected by cluster burn-rate > 2.0.
config_example:
# breaker rule example
scope: model:resnet-34
min_samples: 500
window_sec: 120
incident_threshold: 0.25
burn_rate_multiplier: 1.5
probe_schedule: [0.1, 1, 10, 100]
fallback_priority: ['cache', 'quantized_variant', 'regional_model', 'fail_open']
// note: percentages are traffic percent (0.1 means 0.1% of traffic)
testing_plan: 1) Unit tests for smoothing and incident_score math; 2) Integration tests in dev cluster: simulate spike shapes (burst errors, slow drift latency, multi-tenant correlated surge); 3) Chaos test in staging: inject dependency failures in one region and validate staged rejoin behavior; 4) Canary rollout: dark-launch rules for 48h, then enable for <5 high-risk tenants, monitor burn-rate and alert noise; 5) Load test with synthetic tenants to verify sample thresholds behave as expected.
monitoring_and_alerting: - New SLO-aware alerts: when trip confidence > 0.9 for any tenant/model AND estimated SLO burn-rate > 1.2x -> P1 on-call alert. - Dashboards: per-scope heatmap of incident_score and confidence, rejoin progress column, fallback hit-rate, and regional reroute counts. - Instrumentation: traces include breaker_reason and last_probe_result; metrics: breaker_trips_total{scope,reason}, breaker_probe_success_ratio, fallback_used_total. - Runbooks and playbooks updated with step-by-step rollback and manual untrip commands.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (dark): deploy feature flagged with metrics-only for 2 weeks, validate signals. Phase 2 (canary): enable for 3 low-volume tenants for 1 week. Phase 3 (gradual): enable on percentage basis across regions with telemetry gates. Phase 4: global enable with 24/7 watch and automated fallback adjustments. Final: document in Console release notes and add customer-facing guidance for enterprise tenants.
risks_and_mitigation: - Risk: mis-calibrated min_samples causes slow reaction; mitigate with simulated traffic and safety lower bound that allows manual override. - Risk: staged probes amplify load on healthy dependencies; mitigate with probe isolation quotas and negative cache for immediate failures. - Risk: fallback quality mismatch may degrade UX; mitigate by prioritizing compatible quantized variants and clearly emitting fallback metadata to callers so the app can surface notices. - Risk: high-cardinality metrics blow up TSDB; mitigate with sampling/rollup and pre-aggregation per 1m buckets.
